note: Re-judged 2026-10-26 at HEAD 36a89bf4c6 (independent judge, clean clone, go -overlay, tree untouched), after bb90bdec23, 41eeb0fea4, 4287e22441 and a751d4580b. RFC 3948 Section 5.1: "Because SGW will now see two possible SAs that lead to 10.1.2.3, it can become confused about where to send packets coming from Suzy's server.  Implementors MUST devise ways of preventing this from occurring." BOTH EARLIER FINDINGS ARE FIXED. Tunnel vs transport: transport-mode Child SAs are now recorded and conflictLocked compares a tunnel with a transport pair either way round; skipping that comparison reddens TestRFC3948TunnelAroundTransportPeerRefused, TestRFC3948TunnelAroundTransportPeerInstallBackstop and TestRFC3948OrderedTransportEqualPriorityRefused; not recording transport pairs reddens those plus TestRFC3948OrderedTransportBesideFullTunnelServed. Operator-fixed classification: p operatorFixed always -> PeerChosenAgainstFixed, NarrowedProtocol, NarrowedPort red; h operatorFixed always -> FixedAgainstPeerChosen red; sameInnerSelector protocol / port / prefix comparison dropped -> NarrowedProtocol / NarrowedPort / NarrowedByPeerDistinctPriority red; priority ignored -> ConfiguredOverlapEqualPriority and OrderedTransportEqualPriority red; configured-host clause off -> OrderedTransportBesideFullTunnelServed red. Re-probed and still red: PolicySelectorsOverlap never true (21 tagged units), install claim check skipped (4), narrowing filter off (2, install backstop holds the rest), responder wiring nil (4), both IKE SA rekey inheritances nil (2 each), Child SA rekey innerGuard dropped (RekeyedChildKeepsInnerAddress), strand turned into release (FailedPolicyRemovalKeepsRecord, StrandedRecordRefusesOverlap), pool substitution off (TwoPeersSameRequestedAddressDistinctLeases, ZeInitiatedRekeyNamesOnlyTheLease), answerNamesOnlyLeases off (ZeInitiatedRekeyNamesOnlyTheLease). THE CODE IS CORRECT on every path probed: scratch tests at HEAD showed a tunnel peer configured 0.0.0.0/0 that narrows to 198.18.0.9/32 is refused beside an ordered transport host in both orders, a transport peer choosing a host other than its configured remote address is refused beside a configured tunnel at distinct priorities in both orders, and 16 concurrent installs of one inner address record exactly one. WHY STILL WEAK, the tests do not prove three of those guards. Finding 1 (the exemption's transport half): classifyInnerPair's exact-host test (isConfiguredHost) is proven by no test. Replacing it with operatorFixed = true for every transport pair leaves the whole scoped set green, tagged and untagged (-race), because every transport unit's pair is the peer's configured host or runs at equal priority. Scenario under that break: transport peer b (remote-address 198.18.0.9, no selector, policy-priority 1000, no NAT, so no substitution) proposes transport TSi 10.1.2.3/32, TSr 192.0.2.1/32 beside tunnel peer a holding its configured 10.1.2.0/24 at 2000; both are served and two SAs lead to 10.1.2.3, the address b chose. Fix: a negative unit tagged RFC3948-5.1-1 running that case in both orders at distinct priorities, with a mutant record on the isConfiguredHost line. Finding 2 (concurrent responders): releasing both retryMu and mu between conflictLocked and putLocked in innerSelectorRegistry.claim leaves every tagged and untagged unit green; a scratch stress test (16 unbound peers past narrowing for 10.1.2.3/32 calling createFirstChildSA at once) records 2 holdings in round 0. Every tagged backstop unit installs sequentially, so the atomicity that keeps two concurrent responders apart is unproven. Fix: a negative unit tagged RFC3948-5.1-1 doing that concurrent install and asserting one holding and one served dataplane, with a mutant record. Finding 3 (initiator wiring unit races): TestRFC3948InitiatorSessionRefusesHeldInnerAddress waits for ps.ownedSA != nil and then reads ps.getChildSA() once, but maintainSA stores ownedSA (established.go) before initiatorFirstChildSA decides the Child SA, so the read can see nil before the decision. With runInitiator's sa.innerSelectors assignment removed (fsm.go), the unit passed 1 of 36 runs, then 1 of 100 at -cpu=4: a false green. Fix: wait for the decision itself (a Child SA adopted, or the refusal path's childCreate start), not for ownedSA. Minor, not counted: classifyInnerPair's `if p.transport()` (configured host applies to transport pairs only) is unproven: applying it to tunnels too leaves the set green and lets tunnel peer a (remote 198.18.0.7, prio 1000) proposing its own outer address 198.18.0.7/32 as inner sit beside configured 198.18.0.0/24 at 2000. Not counted because the address so exempted is one the operator wrote (the peer's own remote-address), so the break admits an ordered overlap of an operator-written address, not of a peer-chosen one; it still departs from the stated rule that a tunnel pair is fixed only by a configured selector. BUILD AT HEAD: internal/component/ike/engine does not compile its tests at HEAD (ike_auth_algorithms_test.go uses ikecrypto.ENCR_CHACHA20_POLY1305, which exists only in the uncommitted working-tree crypto/transform.go; committed by e1467639d8), so ./le rfc check reports the package's 292 tagged requirements as not evidence; every run above overlaid that one file away.
